svg.title: Same five stars, different institutional rules
svg.desc: An original comparison diagram showing how two five-star reputation systems can attach different institutional meanings to similar-looking ratings. Airbnb guest ratings group four and five stars as positive and one through three as negative in host-facing displays, while Uber driver ratings are averaged over the most recent 500 rated trips and compared with a city-specific minimum that can affect account access after warnings. A bottom panel emphasizes that the visible star is an input, not the full rule.
svg.text: Same five stars. Different institutional rules.
The visible scale is only the front end. Aggregation, thresholds, labels, and downstream consequences define what the score actually means.
Airbnb guest ratings
Published guest-review documentation
4–5 stars
Displayed to future hosts as positive ratings
1–3 stars
Displayed to future hosts with a warning indicator
Ratings can also inform booking acceptance, Instant Book
eligibility, guest-status decisions, warnings, or removal.
Uber driver ratings
Published community and driver documentation
Rolling average
Most recent 500 rated trips, or all if fewer
City-specific minimum
Falling below it after warnings can affect access
Uber also documents protections that can exclude some
ratings tied to factors outside a driver's control.
The star is an input, not the contract.
Two interfaces can both say “1 to 5” while encoding different categories, memory windows, thresholds, remedies, and consequences.
Policies vary by market and change over time. This figure summarizes published platform documentation current to September 2026; no platform interface artwork is reproduced.
